query.sql: SELECT * FROM (VALUES (1, 'Resolved self_spectrum setting', 'Absent', 'Absent', 'Version 2 therefore applies its default: enabled.'), (2, 'Runtime family artifact version', '1', '2', 'The objective definition changed between executions.'), (3, 'Before: same-frequency raw loss', '0.029012952', '0.029012952', 'Exactly equal on the controlled source batch.'), (4, 'Before: cross-frequency raw loss', '0.032264613', '0.032264613', 'Exactly equal on the controlled source batch.'), (5, 'Before: self-spectrum raw loss', 'Not evaluated', '3651.502686', 'New term is the discontinuity.'), (6, 'Median training cross-spectrum raw loss', '0.001856', '37.5369', 'New median includes the dominant self term; totals are not definition-compatible.'), (7, 'Median calibrated family gradient ratio', '1.25× cross/global', '39.3× cross/global', 'The added term overwhelms family balancing; windows are 5000 versus 25 epochs.'), (8, 'Data retention enabled', 'true', 'false', 'Explains loss of data-gradient stabilization, not the initial before-evaluation jump.'), (9, 'New-run native data loss', 'N/A', '0.1524 → 0.3303', 'Reconstruction fidelity is degrading through epoch 25.')) AS t("order", metric, old_run, new_run, interpretation) ORDER BY "order"
query.description: Read the two resolved configurations, environment manifests, calibration artifacts, pre-training evaluations, and JSONL histories; compare immutable settings and component-level scalars.
filters: Pre-training comparison uses the fixed before.json evaluation in each run.
Latest training comparison is limited to completed epoch 25 in the active no-data-retention run.
Only enabled cross-spectrum component scalars are included.
metric_definitions: Cross-spectrum raw family loss is the sum of enabled component raw scalars after their inner weights and before the family calibration scale.
Self-term share is self_spectrum.auto_spectrum raw scalar divided by cross_spectrum raw family scalar.
Paired-term delta is the maximum absolute old-versus-new difference across same_frequency and cross_frequency on before.json.

query.sql: WITH old_run AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('cases/turbulent_combustion/runs/coherence_fix_AB_balanced/20260829T235221Z_b3b586c4/evaluation/before.json')), new_run AS (SELECT * FROM read_json_auto('cases/turbulent_combustion/runs/coherence_fix_AB_no_data_retention/20260831T222923Z_f6c4f1ca/evaluation/before.json')) SELECT greatest(abs(new_run.coherence.components."cross_spectrum.same_frequency.magnitude_squared" - old_run.coherence.components."cross_spectrum.same_frequency.magnitude_squared"), abs(new_run.coherence.components."cross_spectrum.cross_frequency.band_energy_coupling" - old_run.coherence.components."cross_spectrum.cross_frequency.band_energy_coupling")) AS paired_term_max_delta FROM old_run CROSS JOIN new_run
query.description: Component scalars from evaluation/before.json for the two runs, evaluated from the same source checkpoint and fixed sample IDs.
metric_definitions: Paired-term delta is max(abs(new same-frequency - old same-frequency), abs(new cross-frequency - old cross-frequency)).

query.sql: WITH h AS (SELECT * FROM read_ndjson_auto('cases/turbulent_combustion/runs/coherence_fix_AB_no_data_retention/20260831T222923Z_f6c4f1ca/metrics/history.jsonl') WHERE epoch_complete = true AND epoch = 25), c AS (SELECT h.*, v.component, v.component_key, v.raw_loss, v.weighted_contribution FROM h CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES ('Self spectrum', 'self_spectrum.auto_spectrum', h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/self_spectrum.auto_spectrum/raw", h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/self_spectrum.auto_spectrum/weighted_contribution"), ('Same frequency', 'same_frequency.magnitude_squared', h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/same_frequency.magnitude_squared/raw", h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/same_frequency.magnitude_squared/weighted_contribution"), ('Cross frequency', 'cross_frequency.band_energy_coupling', h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/cross_frequency.band_energy_coupling/raw", h."coherence_component/cross_spectrum/cross_frequency.band_energy_coupling/weighted_contribution")) v(component, component_key, raw_loss, weighted_contribution)) SELECT component, component_key, raw_loss, raw_loss / "coherence_family/cross_spectrum/raw" AS share, weighted_contribution, "coherence_family/cross_spectrum/calibration_scale" AS calibration_scale, epoch, "coherence_family/cross_spectrum/raw" AS family_raw_loss, 'running' AS run_status FROM c
query.description: The latest complete epoch record was selected and its three cross-spectrum component raw losses were divided by the raw family total.
metric_definitions: Component share = component raw loss / cross-spectrum family raw loss.

query.sql: SELECT median(family_gradient_diagnostics.family_gradient_norms.cross_spectrum * "coherence_family/cross_spectrum/calibration_scale" / (family_gradient_diagnostics.family_gradient_norms.global_distribution * "coherence_family/global_distribution/calibration_scale")) AS gradient_ratio FROM read_ndjson_auto('cases/turbulent_combustion/runs/coherence_fix_AB_no_data_retention/20260831T222923Z_f6c4f1ca/metrics/history.jsonl') WHERE epoch_complete = true AND epoch <= 25
query.description: Family gradient norms and calibration scales recorded for each of the first 25 completed epochs.
metric_definitions: Per-epoch gradient imbalance = (cross-spectrum raw family gradient norm × cross-spectrum calibration scale) / (global-distribution raw family gradient norm × global-distribution calibration scale); headline value is the median across 25 epochs.

blocks.body: # Cross-spectrum loss jump: controlled run audit

## Executive Summary

The high value is caused by a **metric-definition/configuration change**, not by a change in the same-frequency or cross-frequency formulas. The newer runtime adds `self_spectrum.auto_spectrum`; because the archived launch configuration omitted that key, version 2 defaulted it to enabled. At epoch 25, this term supplies 99.986% of the raw cross-spectrum family loss. The current edit in `AB_balanced.yaml` did not affect this run because it was launched from the older run's archived `resolved_config.yaml`.

The plotted quantity is an unbounded loss/objective, not a 0–100% coherence score: larger is worse. The run is still active and has no final reconstruction-set comparison yet.

## The newly enabled self term explains essentially the entire jump

On the same pre-training source checkpoint and fixed evaluation batch, both paired terms are numerically identical across runs: same-frequency is 0.029012952 and cross-frequency is 0.032264613. Only the new run evaluates the self-spectrum term, at 3651.502686. This rules out a revised paired-coherence formula as the primary cause.

## Controlled comparison and runtime evidence

The immutable resolved configurations differ only in the experiment name and `objectives.data_retention.enabled`; neither archived configuration contains a `self_spectrum` entry. The runtime artifacts identify cross-spectrum family version 1 for the older run and version 2 for the newer run. Version 2 treats every omitted component except `band_energy` as enabled.

## Root cause and secondary effect

The launch reused `coherence_fix_AB_balanced/.../resolved_config.yaml`, then overrode only data retention. Your later `AB_balanced.yaml` edit is valid, but it is not an input to that already-launched run. With the key absent, `family.py` applies `default_enabled = key != "band_energy"`, activating `self_spectrum`.

The large auto-spectrum loss also distorts family balancing. Across the first 25 epochs, the median calibrated cross-spectrum gradient is about 39.3× the calibrated global-distribution gradient; the latter is already at its scale cap of 100. Disabling data retention did not create the initial jump—the controlled `before.json` already contains it—but it removes the stabilizing data gradient and the native data loss rises from 0.1524 to 0.3303 through epoch 25.

## Recommended action

Treat the current run as a different objective, not as a clean no-data-retention ablation. To reproduce the historical paired-only cross-spectrum objective, relaunch with both overrides made explicit:

```bash
python cases/turbulent_combustion/run.py post-train \
  --config runs/coherence_fix_AB_balanced/20260829T235221Z_b3b586c4/resolved_config.yaml \
  --override objectives.data_retention.enabled=false \
  --override coherence.families.cross_spectrum.components.self_spectrum.enabled=false \
  --override output.experiment_name=coherence_fix_AB_no_data_retention_no_self_spectrum
```

The `weight: 1.0` value is harmless when `enabled: false`; the explicit override is what matters for an archived-config launch.

## Limitations

The newer run was still marked `running` at epoch 25 when this snapshot was taken, so no final reconstruction-set coherence score is available. The two environment manifests also report dirty worktrees; commit IDs alone cannot reconstruct uncommitted source state. Runtime family artifacts, identical paired-term values on the controlled pre-training batch, and the emitted self-term history nevertheless provide direct evidence of the executed semantics.

## Source notes

Evidence comes from each run's immutable `resolved_config.yaml`, `environment.json`, `evaluation/before.json`, calibration artifact, and `metrics/history.jsonl`, plus the current cross-spectrum family implementation. The chart uses the latest completed epoch only; the table preserves exact values where direct lookup matters.
